samples.summary: The slim/mobile docs toolbar's reset→`undefined` change has no test; only the shared `TextFormatGroup` is covered
samples.evidence: The diff changes two independent toolbars to pass `undefined` on reset: `text-format-group.tsx` (covered by the new `packages/frontend/tests/components/text-formatting/color-reset.test.ts`) and `docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx` lines 490/512 (`onReset={() => handleTextColor(undefined)}` / `handleHighlightColor(undefined)`), which no test touches. Grepping for `DocsFormattingToolbar` in packages/frontend finds only src files (App.tsx, docs-detail.tsx, shared-document.tsx, harness/hunt/page.tsx) — no test file — so a regression back to `""` in the slim toolbar would ship green.

samples.summary: `markerToXml`'s new buClr guard (drop a cleared/unexpressible marker color) is untested
samples.evidence: `markerToXml` changed from `if (marker.color != null)` to emitting only when `storedColorToThemeColor(marker.color)` is truthy, so a marker color of `''`, `'red'` or `rgb(...)` now behaves differently (dropped / normalized). No export test constructs a `block.marker`: grep for `marker:`/`buClr` under packages/slides/test/export returns nothing, and the only marker coverage is the round-trip fixture (`build-rich-pptx.ts`, buClr `#FF0000`), which exercises only the already-working hex path. The new `#728` PPTX tests use `para(...)` (paragraph inlines), never a marker.

samples.summary: No test verifies the premise of the fix — that `applyStyle({ color: undefined })` actually removes the color attribute from the CRDT
samples.evidence: Both toolbar comments assert "the store turns an explicitly-undefined key into an attribute removal". The mechanism is `removedInlineStyleAttrs` + `removeStyleByPath` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:144-163, 1876-1882), whose existing test coverage (per docs/tasks/archive/.../20260526-docs-unlink-href-todo.md) is for `href` only. The new frontend test stops at `expect(editor.applyStyle).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ color: undefined })` — a mock-call assertion that cannot detect the color attribute surviving in the tree. I found no test in packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts asserting color/backgroundColor removal.

samples.summary: PDF export still resolves colors with bare `defaultColorResolver` and no test covers the `''`/CSS-string input class there
samples.evidence: The change normalizes DOCX and PPTX sinks via `toRgbHexColor`, but `pdf-style-map.ts:144` (`const resolved = defaultColorResolver(hex);`) was left on the raw resolver and no test in this diff feeds it the legacy `''` or an `rgb(...)` value that HTML paste can store. Same for the inline/cell background paint paths (`paint-layout.ts:234/289/422`, `table-renderer.ts:175/224`), which still call the resolver directly — those are truthiness-guarded, but the pre-resolver `''`→`undefined` normalization the helper's doc comment argues is essential for theme-aware resolvers is neither applied nor tested there.

samples.summary: The cell-fill test only inspects word/document.xml although the code comment claims header1.xml/footer1.xml are the same sink
samples.evidence: The new exporter comment names `document.xml / header1.xml / footer1.xml` as the sinks, but the test reads only `zip.file('word/document.xml')`. A table cell background inside a header/footer is never asserted, so a header/footer path that bypassed `toDocxHexColor` would pass.

samples.summary: `toRgbHexColor` has untested input shapes that silently drop a visible color (space-separated modern CSS, `#RGBA`, unparseable alpha)
samples.evidence: The rgb regex only accepts the comma form, so `rgb(0 128 255 / 50%)` and `#1234` (4-digit RGBA) fall through to `undefined`, and `isTransparentAlpha` on an unparseable alpha (`rgba(1,2,3,var(--a))`) takes the 'treated as opaque' branch. None of these appear in packages/docs/test/model/color.test.ts or docx-style-map.test.ts, so the documented intent (never drop a color the user can see) is unverified for them.
